text: Open with an everyday lapse in recall, not a medical claim. This is a relatable motivation, not evidence that an EEG detector identifies forgetting. Transition to the concept film.

Play the embedded 36-second concept film with sound. It illustrates the intended wearable experience, using the approved mannequin and revised desk reaction. The neural strengths shown in the film are illustrative story values. The running prototype uses the phone camera and supports synthetic EEG replay plus a Crown adapter.

text: Hardware concept: Neurosity Crown for sensing EEG and Ray-Ban Meta glasses for first-person context, supported by the Memorypalace app. Crown is an EEG sensor, not a neurostimulation device; Ray-Ban Meta glasses are not Meta Quest. The current working recorder is an Android phone camera, with a Crown stream adapter. Twenty minutes is the requested onboarding target, not a measured result; code baseline currently uses 120 seconds. Sources: hardware-demo/eegdemo/pipeline.py; hardware-demo/README.md; https://neurosity.co/crown ; https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/dat/build-integration-android/

text: Current implementation: clean frontal EEG, theta (4–8 Hz) over alpha (8–13 Hz) band power, four-second non-overlapping windows, per-wearer z-score, threshold 2.0, four consecutive elevated windows. It measures a sustained load proxy. Phase-shift detection is not present in the inspected implementation; avoid describing this method as phase-shift inference or as a state-of-the-art benchmark. Source: confusion-detector/src/config.py; confusion-detector/src/cognitive_load.py; hardware-demo/eegdemo/pipeline.py.

text: The three raw EEG traces and 20 / 40 / 70 microvolt ranges are synthetic illustrations, not measured people or diagnostic norms. Peak-to-peak means maximum minus minimum; raw amplitude also depends on recording conditions. The live prototype calibrates theta/alpha mean and spread over 120 seconds, then uses a z-score. It does not trigger from raw peak-to-peak amplitude. Person icon: Lucide user-round, https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/blob/main/icons/user-round.svg (ISC).

text: Four consecutive windows above z=2.0 are required. No overlap means samples are not reused; it does not prove statistical independence of brain activity. The active backend finalizes an ongoing recording on this trigger, attaches the signal context, and saves it. The concept film illustrates the broader event-capture vision. Sources: confusion-detector/src/config.py; hardware-demo/eegdemo/server.py Runtime.trigger.

text: Controlled comparison reported in confusion-detector/README.md, The one result that matters: 4-second windows, 75% overlap (hop 1s) 30.3 false alarms/hour; 50% overlap (hop 2s) 18.9; no overlap (hop 4s) 1.3. Same stationary synthetic fixture and threshold. Do not generalize the absolute rate to people or drifting baselines; the drifting fixture reported 7.2/hour at the default setting. This chart is engineering evidence for avoiding repeated samples, not a clinical performance claim.

text: Voloridge asked for signal out of public data. Ours is EEG: 28 channels, five people, fifteen sessions from Shin et al. 2018 dataset A. Regress out eye-channel contributions, measure three band powers, logistic regression, one moving average. Alternatives were paired against their own baselines on the same recordings, windows and calibration folds. They lost or tied; these rows are not a cross-participant leaderboard. The one retained addition is a smoothing half-life. Source: presentation/SLIDES-VOLORIDGE.md and eeg-state-detection/README.md. Public-data research, distinct from the running four-window prototype detector.

text: Models were frozen and SHA-256 hashed before held-out blocks. Per session: first six blocks calibrate, last three score. The circular time-shift null preserves autocorrelation; shuffled windows would break it. 2,000 shifts per session. Eight of 15 sessions beat that null at nominal p ≤ 0.05 (session-wise, not multiplicity corrected). Orange diamonds are the identical pipeline on eye channels; two participants show substantial ocular contribution. The same null discipline rejected the brief-event zigzag result: 6/36 versus a 2/36 baseline, p=0.13 against random flags. Sources: eeg-state-detection/README.md; outputs/backtest_state/report.json; outputs/burst_diagnostic_dev/report.json. This is offline task/rest detection, not real-world forgetting or emotion accuracy.
